'''David Mark Haddleton''' (born 1962) is a professor in the department of chemistry at the [[University of Warwick]]. His work focuses on controlled polymer synthesis and the industrial applications of polymer materials. He is a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]].

== Career ==
Haddleton was editor in chief of the ''[[European Polymer Journal]]'' from 2002 – 2009 prior to becoming the founding editor and editor in chief of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Polymer Chemistry from 2009 to 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/events/97881/prof-david-haddleton-warwick/|title=Prof David Haddleton (Warwick)|publisher=Imperial College London|website=Imperial College London|access-date=2026-10-21}}</ref> He is the executive editor in chief of Cambridge Materials journals published by Cambridge University Press (CUP).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cambridge Materials |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/publications/collections/cambridge-materials |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=Cambridge Core |language=en}}</ref> He has founded two companies Warwick Effect Polymers Ltd (now part of Abzena) a drug-polymer conjugation company and Medherant Ltd which develops transdermal drug delivery patches for delivery of testosterone for women<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Medherant |date=2025-03-03 |title=Innovative patch technology for transdermal drug delivery |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d43747-025-00012-6 |journal=Biopharma Dealmakers |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |doi=10.1038/d43747-025-00012-6 |issn=2730-6283}} </ref> where he is a director and CSO.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://warwick.ac.uk/newsandevents/pressreleases/researchers_create_world146s/ |title=Researchers create World's first ibuprofen patch - delivering pain relief directly through skin|publisher=Warwick University |access-date=28 January 2022}}</ref>
